findings.text: This is a legitimate RETROSPECTIVE dogfood and is honestly labeled as such. The manifest assumptions, the WARP-0112 spec (Intent/Context/Out-of-scope), and PLAN-0002 all state the companion home was ALREADY delivered in the tripdesk product and the layer expresses/verifies it now; 'delivered through the layer' is never allowed to imply the code was BUILT through the layer. Journeys are correctly labeled API-level (not the W5/W7 UI runners), and WARP-0201..0204 are labeled retrospective specs whose proof-of-delivery is the shared live journey suite, not per-spec verdicts. No material overclaim.

WARP-0202 AC2 (anti-shadowing) is honestly evidenced by code ordering, not a fabricated live test: the spec explicitly says AC2 is evidenced by the _auto_select code plus live owner-scoping, and constructing synthetic shadowing fixtures is out of scope. I read the real product code (tripdesk_app/views.py HomeSummaryView._auto_select) and confirmed it implements and documents exactly the claimed priority (dated-window-contains-today > open-ended-started > soonest-upcoming > most-recent) with the shadowing-bug-fix rationale. The claim is truthful.

Minor imprecision, not blocking: the manifest's docs check says company references appear 'never in docs/ or plugin/'. The repo slug 'Bcengi/warp' does appear in docs/plugin.md and author 'Dmitry Grinberg' in docs/manifest.yaml, but the genericity sweep (scripts/check_docs.sh) explicitly strips the repo's own distribution coordinate and forbids only product/company names (bcengi/tripdesk/travelpass/workpass/agentpass/coreconnect/companion/mvne), exempting docs/design and docs/research as provenance. The substantive product references do not leak into generic docs; the sweep passes. Benign shorthand.

Minor, not blocking: PLAN-0002 lists 4 regression journeys (CJ1-CJ4) while the runner executes 5 (CJ3 is split into CJ3a foreign-404 and CJ3b zero-trip-200-phase-none, the two assertions CJ3 names). A benign execution split, not a DAG or coverage hole.

summary: Genuine 1.0 receipt, PASS. I reproduced everything from scratch: validate.py all exits 0; PLAN-0002 is a real (non-stub) plan with intact two-way mirroring and an acyclic ordered DAG; I ran the journey runner and independently curled the live backend, confirming 5/5 journeys reflect real, non-vacuous behavior (200 all sections owner-scoped under budget, 401, 404, phase none) and the timing budget is real; verify.sh is GATE GREEN with 0 undeclared and the git show file stat proves ZERO product code was changed; PLAN-0001 is revision 4 with D1 resolved, 11/12 shipped, W12 the sole frontier, run-check clear, and shipping W12 makes it 12/12 releasable. proof_digest recomputes to sha256:03e9cbd564cfb178, matching the manifest. The dogfood is an honestly-labeled retrospective: it verifies an already-delivered feature via live API journeys without touching product code, and the specs' ACs (including WARP-0202's code-evidenced anti-shadowing) match real backend behavior. No theater, no overclaim, no blocking findings.
